analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: DSY CMD guide debates; Semis sentiment fragile; BIS rule; Zegona inline; Springer beats; Agency tracker 17 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities fell on 16 Nov, led by tech and AI: NVDA -4.5%, DRAM -6%, SMH -5%, neoclouds -7%. Sentiment is fragile after Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, tighter US chip-export rules, caution ahead of Nvidia earnings, and a negative SemiAnalysis report. Investors may also be making room for an upcoming IPO.

The sell-off extended into Asia. MSCI's regional equity gauge fell as much as 1.5%, heading for its lowest close since early April, with Taiwan and South Korea leading declines. Alibaba fell as much as 5.6%, Baidu 6.6%, Hang Seng Tech -2.3%, and Minimax and Z.AI (Zhipu) each lost more than 6%.

A new BIS rule, released 16 Nov, tightens US AI-chip export controls to stop Chinese companies from renting computing power at overseas data centres. It rescinds the unenforced AI Diffusion Rule, adds licensing requirements for advanced chips and servers used for substantial compute capacity for Chinese and other restricted companies, and adds chip-export licensing for Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Licences are case by case.

GS expects the BIS rule to raise compliance costs and uncertainty for chip suppliers and cloud operators, and to delay affected chip shipments and data-centre projects. It is not a blanket ban on overseas AI investment. Tighter compute access is a risk to AI model training and Chinese cloud revenue growth.
Semis investor questions have turned cautious, with bulls asking at what point the falls price things in. Focus has shifted to 2028 and beyond rather than 2026-27.

SemiAnalysis's latest accelerator model cut its 2028 accelerator spending forecast by 28%, with sharper cuts in later years, left 2026 largely unchanged and put most of the downside on Nvidia. GS notes its forecasts were well above Street estimates.

Ahead of Nvidia results on the evening of 17 Nov, a minority see downside risk to guidance. Most see limited near-term risk and focus on how the company addresses CEO succession. The bigger debate is calendar 2028.

Zegona: revenue beat and EBITDAaL missed the Street by 0.7%. Revenue was in line with GIR at +4.4% y/y. Lower capex from lower churn lifted FCF above the Street. Net adds were +9k broadband and 298k mobile. Messaging is unchanged.

Springer Nature Q3 beat and raise: operating profit 2% ahead of expectations, FY26 underlying revenue growth guidance raised to 6%+ from around 6%. Nine-month underlying revenue grew 6.3% vs GS/company-compiled consensus of 6.1%/6.0%. Implied Q3 underlying growth is about 6.5% vs 6.2% in Q2, led by Research at about 7.8%.

Springer Nature nine-month adjusted operating profit rose 7.7% underlying to €428mn, with margin up 50bps to 29.1%. FCF rose €69mn to €244mn, helped by a one-off FX derivative settlement benefit. Net debt/EBITDA was 1.6x.

Dassault Systemes (DSY) CMD: the 2029 guide is reiterated with no pushout. It now gives absolute targets: double-digit revenue and EPS growth in 2029, revenue above €8B (in line with Street) and non-IFRS diluted EPS of €1.80 (Street €1.72, about 5% ahead). OFCF is guided to €2.5bn, 5% above Street.

GS reads the DSY headline as implying mid-single-digit upgrades to out-year Street numbers. The debate is the shape of growth, whether it is back-end loaded and assumes acceleration, and clarity on 2027 (Street at 7% growth, 5.5% ex M&A). GS first read is flat to up. EPS growth is about 4% in 2026 and 8% in 2027 and 2028, slower than PCOR/ADSK/VEEV, at a premium valuation.

SAP Chief Customer Officer Thomas Saueressig is leaving and stays until end of March 2027. Emmanuel Raptopoulos takes over his responsibilities on an interim basis from January 2027. Sinch named CFO Jonas Dahlberg as CEO with immediate effect.

Global ad agency tracker after 3Q26 points to stable ad markets. Publicis leads media net wins at about $5bn YTD despite losing Coca-Cola in North America, Omnicom about $2bn, and WPP about a $1bn net loss. In creative, WPP and Stagwell had strong years, Publicis faces a small headwind into 2027 and Omnicom a larger one.

GS estimates imply about 6% growth in top-100 advertisers' marketing expenses in 2026, with 2027 slightly higher. GS's regression model predicted the Q3 organic growth beat (actual 2.9%, model 2.2%, consensus 1.5%) and points to Q4 acceleration to 3.1% vs 2.7% consensus. Six listed consultancies reported 5.7% constant-currency growth in Q3 vs 4.2% in Q2, a positive read for Publicis' Sapient.

A Milan court placed Revolut's Italian operations under one-year judicial administration over anti-money-laundering control failures. Revolut itself is not under investigation. It must implement a 15-point remediation plan.

GS HBM tracker: expectations are improving, especially for SK Hynix, with consensus raising pricing, shipment, revenue and operating profit forecasts over the past month. Japanese plastic-film imports to key Samsung sites are up 51% y/y through October. GS's Samsung HBM ASP forecasts are 19% above consensus for 2027 and 7% above for 2028.
A 10-20% foundry price hike could cut ASIC margin by 4-5 ppts, excluding OSAT. GUC Q3 margin was 20.6% vs 24.2% a year earlier, and Alchip's 18% was its lowest in 3 years.
Adyen partnered with OVO to process 100% of its consumer card payments, about 3.5m households, its first major UK utility win.
Moody's downgraded VMED O2's CFR to B2 from B1, outlook stable.

Dentsu Q3 organic revenue fell 3.7% and operating margin was 10.5%, both below August expectations. FY organic guidance was cut to about -1% from 0-1%, with margin guidance maintained in the 13% range. Americas is now expected at -5-6% and EMEA at about -2%.
Google faces a potential new EU antitrust setback: on 12 Nov an adviser to the EU's highest court recommended overturning a 2024 judgment that annulled a €1.49bn AdSense fine.

GS trading desk: activity was 4 out of 10, with muted asset manager and hedge fund flows. Staples saw a flight to safety, helped by reversion after heavy short supply. TSCO +4%, BBWI -9%, VSXY -5%, ARMK +1% on EPS.

Derivatives: the S&P realized its entire weekly implied move, with QQQ and IWM close behind, driving a jump in vol and skew. Index options are expensive. Option volumes were muted. The desk saw buying of capped upside in AMZN, MU and TSM and longer-dated downside protection in semis. NVDA carries a 7.8% implied 1-day move, and the S&P straddle for the rest of the week at 2% looks underpriced to GS.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA fell 4.5% on Huang's departure, export rule tightening and the SemiAnalysis forecast cuts. Earnings are due the evening of 17 Nov, with a 7.8% implied 1-day move.
Springer Nature Q3 beat and raise, with FY26 underlying revenue growth guidance lifted to 6%+.
Dentsu cut FY organic growth guidance to about -1% after Q3 organic revenue fell 3.7%, below expectations.
Dassault Systemes reiterated its 2029 targets at its CMD with no pushout, with EPS of €1.80 about 5% above the Street.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment is fragile and the debate has moved to 2028. Most investors see limited near-term risk into Nvidia results. GS HBM tracker is positive on SK Hynix and Samsung.
The group saw flight-to-safety buying on 16 Nov, helped by reversion after heavy short supply per GS PB.
Ad markets are stable, with media account wins favouring Publicis and Omnicom, and WPP at a net loss.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports results on the evening of 17 Nov. A minority see downside risk to guidance, most see limited near-term risk, and investors focus on CEO succession commentary. Implied 1-day move is 7.8%.
Zegona (reported 17 Nov): revenue beat and EBITDAaL 0.7% below Street. Revenue growth was +4.4% y/y, in line with GIR. FCF beat on lower capex.

Springer Nature Q3 (reported): operating profit 2% ahead of expectations. Nine-month underlying revenue growth was 6.3% vs GS 6.1% and company-compiled consensus 6.0%. Adjusted operating profit was €428mn (+7.7% underlying), margin 29.1%. FY26 underlying revenue growth guidance was raised to 6%+ from around 6% (GS/Vara consensus 6.1%/6.0%). Underlying adjusted operating margin improvement guidance of more than 30bps was reiterated, vs GS/consensus expectations of 20bps/10bps.

Dentsu Q3 2026 (reported): organic revenue -3.7% and operating margin 10.5%, both below August expectations. Nine-month organic revenue -1.0%, margin 11.8%, slightly ahead of expectations. FY organic growth guidance cut to about -1% from 0-1%, margin guidance kept in the 13% range.
Dassault Systemes CMD targets for 2029 (company guidance, not reported results): revenue above €8B (Street €8bn), non-IFRS diluted EPS of €1.80 (Street €1.72), OFCF of €2.5bn (about 5% above Street).
Ad agency tracker: GS regression model predicted Q3 organic growth of 2.2% vs actual 2.9% and consensus 1.5%. It points to Q4 organic growth of 3.1% vs 2.7% consensus.
Upcoming: NKE investor day on 18 Nov, and earnings from AS, VIK and HD.
risk_factors: Tighter AI chip export controls raise compliance costs and risk delaying chip shipments and data-centre projects.
Longer-term AI accelerator demand, AI monetisation, tighter financing and sustainability of spending are in question, with the debate centred on 2028.
Nvidia CEO succession after Jensen Huang's departure, and the guidance risk at tonight's earnings.
A possible IPO supply overhang as investors make room for an upcoming offering.
S&P straddle for the rest of the week may be underpriced given realized moves.
A foundry price hike of 10-20% could compress ASIC margins.
Google antitrust risk in Europe over the AdSense fine.
vol_and_positioning: The S&P realized its entire weekly implied move on 16 Nov, with QQQ and IWM close behind, causing a jump in vol and skew. Index options are expensive across the board.
Overall option volumes were muted after a week of light positioning and a pickup in ETF short interest.
The desk saw buying of capped upside in AMZN, MU and TSM, and longer-dated outright downside protection in semis.
NVDA has a 7.8% implied 1-day move into earnings. The S&P straddle for the rest of the week is at 2%, which GS says looks underpriced given the current regime.
Floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale, with asset manager and hedge fund flows muted. Short supply across nearly all subsectors was heavier the prior week per GS PB.
geopolitical: The US BIS rule tightens AI-chip export controls to stop Chinese firms accessing offshore compute, and adds licensing for Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
Reports that Congress is moving to pass tighter AI chip export rules.
Chinese AI names fell sharply in Asia: Alibaba, Baidu, Minimax and Z.AI.
